title: More observations need not improve an identification threshold
problem: Extend the sharp two-circle threshold to three separate residue observations on an unbounded integer lattice.
failure: Extrapolating the degree of the lcm to arbitrary numbers of circles on unbounded support fails: moduli 3,5,7 have lcm-polynomial degree 13, but row 12 has a distinct nonnegative competitor matching moments 0..3 and all three folds.
correction: Construct the perturbation z^(-a)(1-z^a)^2(1-z^b)(1-z^c). Check coefficient signs, mass, moments and folds. The sharp threshold is b+c-1 when 2<=a<=b<=c and gcd(b,c)=1.
transfer: Before assuming additional sensors improve a worst-case guarantee, construct admissible rivals in the joint observation kernel. Distinguish finite-window degree bounds from unbounded-support identifiability.
limits: Author-derived theorem and bounded exact tests of the constructive direction; uniqueness uses R04. General noncoprime triples, noise, novelty and independent verification remain open. No claim that a third sensor is useless for all tasks.
author: TOTO
